items.text:
Coaching from first principles: no win rates, no tier lists, no sample sizes.
Every score is my judgment, with the reason beside it.
Your path: Bronze to Masters 450 LP, one rank a season.
Darius top: Plat to Diamond 1. Kog'Maw ADC: Diamond to Masters 450 LP.
Now: low Diamond 4 after decay.
The champion is not your Master to Challenger gap.

A new champion fixes one or two weaknesses. Most of the gap is
decisions: where you stand at minute 14, which wave you push
before dragon, which fights you skip. You already proved the hands
twice.
Dying to assassins is half Kog, half ADC.

Every ADC dies once an assassin reaches them. A dash buys a second
chance, not the first. If you add a dash without changing where
you stand, you will use it to survive the mistake instead of
avoiding it.
Objectives are a timing habit, not a champion.

The team that takes dragon is the one that arrives first, with
waves pushed. Kog does not stop you shoving 60 seconds before
spawn and walking in first. That habit carries to any pick.
One-tricking is your proven system. Keep it.

Two champions, two big climbs, each more than a full tier.
Changing champion is fine. Changing every few weeks, or keeping
three in rotation, is the real risk.
Both of your climbs were on champions with no dash.

Darius and Kog'Maw both win by committing in the right spot. That
may be the style you enjoy. A slippery, dash-heavy champion can
climb and still feel worse to play. Test the feel before you
commit.
Low Diamond is your cheapest place to learn.

LP lost on the way back to Master costs you nothing on the
Challenger run. Learn the new champion here. If it is not second
nature by Master 0 LP, that is your answer.

The only role whose job is the objectives. You
pick every fight. New role for you.

Short walk to both sides. Lots of agency, but a
new role and the deepest champion pool to learn.

Most independent lane, farthest from dragon. You
force objectives by making them answer your side
lane.

Most damage late, least control early. Your agency
runs through a support you did not pick.

• Jungle has the most agency in solo queue: it is the only
role that chooses where every fight happens.
• ADC has the most power late but borrows its agency early.
That is the root of "Kog can't play for objectives".
• Top is the most independent and the farthest from dragon.
• Your two cheap roles are the two you already climbed in.

Kog's hybrid scaling with an escape button.

+ Mobility: E speed (invisible once evolved) and an R
dash.
+ Assassins: R jumps out with a shield; E stealth breaks
their target.
+ Same lane, same waves, same on-hit vs AP build logic
as Kog.

− Still an ADC: early agency runs through your support.
− R needs a mark on an enemy, so it follows your team's
engage.
− Does not fix objectives. That stays a habit to build.
− A pro favourite, so expect bans and balance changes
(my guess).

My pick: Kai'Sa. It fixes two of your three problems
for almost no switch cost, and that saves your time
for the real gap: decisions.
A marksman who owns the map.

+ Objectives become your job: smite, plus ranged DPS on
the pit.
+ Q dash and R (nobody in it dies for a few seconds) for
assassins.
+ Kog's kiting and auto spacing carry over directly.

− A new role: pathing, camp timers and gank reads from
zero.
− Marks reward risky invades; a bad early game snowballs
against you.
− Expect a long stretch below your level. Graves is the
sturdier backup.

Pick Kindred instead if what you are tired of is ADC
itself, your games resting on a support you did not
choose. Accept a slower season for a higher ceiling.
Darius's lane, with a leap and a late game.

+ Q leaps to any unit or ward; E dodges autos and stuns.
+ Assassins do not one-shot a bruiser.
+ Your Darius lane craft (waves, trades, Teleport)
carries over.

− Far from dragon: objectives come from side-lane
pressure, not from being at the pit.
− Top's agency is slow: you can win lane and still lose
the map.
− Your top run ended at Diamond 1, though you have
learned a lot since.

Pick Jax if you miss fighting in a lane where nobody
else matters.

Play each of the three in normals or the
practice tool. After each game, answer one
question: did I want to queue again? Pick the
one you most want to play, not the one that
won.

One champion in ranked. No rotation. Judge it
after 100 ranked games, not after a bad night.
Your two climbs came from exactly this.

• 60 s before dragon or grubs: push, back,
arrive first.
• Before a fight, find their assassins. If you
cannot see them, stand behind your front line,
not beside it.
• Review one loss a day: find your first death
and its cause.

If the new champion feels less natural than
Kog did at the same LP, go back to Kog and
keep the habits. No shame in it: the habits
were the point.

Superseded 2026-11-21: you chose to stay on Kog'Maw.
Kept for the reasoning. Your plan is the "Climb plan"
page.
